summary: Terminal has an unguarded triggerHapticFeedback() call that can silently kill all command handling, plus an unescaped-input XSS in accent/color; search-index fallback covers only 2/10 pages and SW cache-first adds a hidden extra staleness hop; tour resume path skips the page-match check that programmatic nav uses.
result_text: TRACK 3 — Command palette, search index & interactive terminal Repo HEAD reviewed: local clone (main). Scope: assets/js/modules/cmdk.js, terminal.js, tour.js, scripts/extract_index.py. verify.py's 17 checks (incl. search-index sync, JS syntax, tag balance) not re-run. ── SEARCH INDEX: STALENESS WINDOW & FALLBACK COVERAGE ── [medium] Fallback covers only 2 of 10 pages, confirmed via source (not a new discovery, but definitively answers the task question) — assets/js/modules/cmdk.js:47-83, scripts/extract_index.py:11-18 (docstring already documents this). buildSearchIndex() live-scans `#achievementsList .achievement-item` and `#projectsGrid .project-card`; only achievements.html and projects.html render those container IDs. On index/about/experience/journey/contact/privacy/terms/404 (8 pages) the querySelectorAll calls no-op and search relies 100% on SEARCH_STATIC_INDEX with zero runtime augmentation. This is fine as designed — flagging so the "genuinely covers every page" question is answered with certainty, not assumed. [medium] End-to-end staleness window is longer than "next CI run" — three compounding hops, only the first is visible in the repo. (1) .github/workflows/update-search-index.yml:16-19 triggers on `push` to main, not on save/commit — an uncommitted or unpushed local edit to achievements.html/projects.html never reaches the index. (2) The commit-back step (update-search-index.yml:38-47) races stamp-last-commit.yml for the same push event and retries `git pull --rebase` up to 5x with 1-5s sleeps — worst case adds ~25s before the regenerated script.js actually lands on main. (3) Not covered by verify.py's SW check (that check only verifies STATIC_ASSETS entries exist — scripts/verify.py:677-706, no runtime-freshness assertion): sw.js:60-75 serves assets/js/script.js cache-first with background revalidate. A returning visitor with an already-registered SW gets the OLD cached script.js immediately; the revalidation fetch only updates the cache for their *next* load. So even after the CI commit lands, an existing PWA visitor is still one full page-load behind. Net effect: "push → search reflects it" is not a single number, it's push-delay + CI-race (~0-30s) + one stale SW-served visit for already-installed users. Fix suggestion: bump sw.js CACHE_NAME (or move script.js to network-first) whenever update-search-index.yml commits, so the cache invalidates immediately instead of lagging one visit. [nit] Asymmetric automation in the "dual" index: CMDK_PAGES (page-type entries) — cmdk.js:7-26 — has no CI regeneration at all, unlike achievement/project entries. A newly added HTML page won't appear in global search until someone hand-edits this array, and nothing in verify.py enforces CMDK_PAGES-vs-actual-pages parity. Low impact (pages change rarely) but worth a one-line note in extract_index.py's docstring so it doesn't read as "the whole index is automated." [low] cmdk.js:180-187 renderResults() interpolates item.title / item.meta / CMDK_TYPE_LABEL[item.type] into innerHTML unescaped. Data is first-party (site owner's own HTML content via extract_index.py's get_text(), or live textContent), so practical risk is low, but any future achievement/project text containing `<`/`>` would render as raw markup rather than text. Not part of the terminal audit but adjacent to the same file — flagging since I was already in there. Fix suggestion: escape title/meta the same way terminal.js's escapeHtml() does before interpolation. ── TERMINAL: ~15 COMMAND ERROR-HANDLING AUDIT ── [high] terminal.js:253 — `triggerHapticFeedback(10)` is called unconditionally at the very top of execCommand(), before any command lookup, with no `typeof` guard and no try/catch anywhere in the call chain. Compare to radar/resume/whatsnew/tour/theme handlers (lines 42-49, 123-126, 193-200), which all guard their cross-module calls with `typeof X === 'function'`. If haptics.js ever fails to load (blocked script, future module removal, load-order regression), the *first* keystroke on Enter throws a ReferenceError before appendOutput() runs — every command silently stops working, no error line is ever appended (input.value is already cleared at line 273 before execCommand runs), and the user sees nothing happen. Same unconditional call exists in the quickBtns click handler (line 281). Fix suggestion: guard both call sites with `if (typeof triggerHapticFeedback === 'function')`, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in this file. [high] terminal.js:201-215 `accent`/`color` — the "Unknown accent" branch interpolates raw user input into HTML: `` `Unknown accent: '${val}'. ...` `` (line 214), where `val` is only lowercased+trimmed, never escaped, and this string is later inserted via `line.innerHTML =` in appendOutput() (line 238-241). This is DOM XSS reachable by typing/pasting `accent ` into the terminal. The same file already has the correct pattern twice — glossary's not-found branch does `escapeHtml(term)` (line 88), and execCommand's own unknown-command fallback does `escapeHtml(trimmed)` (line 266) — so this is an inconsistency bug, not a missing feature. Self-XSS (requires the victim to enter the payload in their own session, e.g. via a "paste this into the terminal" social-engineering link), but still a real injection point and the exact class of bug the codebase otherwise guards against. Fix suggestion: `escapeHtml(val)` in the error string at line 214. [medium] terminal.js:258-267 execCommand() — no try/catch around `handler(arg)` (line 264). Any handler that throws (including the two issues above, or any future handler) fails silently: the throw happens before appendOutput() is reached, so nothing is echoed and the user gets zero feedback that their command failed. Fix suggestion: wrap the dispatch in try/catch and appendOutput() a generic error line on catch, so a single bad handler can't make the terminal appear unresponsive. [low] terminal.js:185-192 `sound`/`audio` — call `toggleAudioCues()` directly with no `typeof` guard, inconsistent with radar/resume/whatsnew/tour/theme in the same COMMANDS object which all guard equivalent cross-module calls. Currently unreachable in practice (audio.js is in sw.js's STATIC_ASSETS and loads on every page) but inconsistent defensive-coding within one file. Fix suggestion: add the same `typeof` guard for consistency, cheap insurance if the module set ever changes. [low] terminal.js:217-220 `clear` — handled as a special case in execCommand (line 258-261) that calls `COMMANDS.clear()` directly and returns, bypassing appendOutput(). Every other command echoes `visitor@adt:~$ ` before its result; `clear` echoes nothing (the terminal just goes blank with no record the command ran). Minor UX inconsistency, not a functional bug. [nit] terminal.js help text (lines 24-41) lists 15 commands but the COMMANDS object also implements `sound`, `audio`, `tour`, and `color` (alias for `accent`) — 4 working commands undocumented in `help`. Likely intentional easter eggs, but worth confirming that's the intent rather than a doc gap, since `help` is the single source of truth users see. ── TOUR.JS: OVERLAY LIFECYCLE ACROSS PAGE NAVIGATION ── [high] tour.js:337-360 initTour()'s resume-on-load path calls `renderTourStep(idx)` directly (line 357), bypassing the page-match check that tourGoTo() (lines 104-113) uses for programmatic step navigation. tourGoTo() checks `entry.page !== getTourCurrentPage()` and redirects if the step belongs elsewhere; the resume path skips this entirely. Consequence: if a user with an active tour (TOUR_LS_ACTIVE='1' in localStorage survives full-page navigation by design) manually navigates away from the tour's expected page — clicks a random nav link, uses browser back/forward, or types a URL — instead of using Next/Back/Close, the tour resumes on whatever page they land on. renderTourStep()'s `document.querySelector(entry.sel) || document.body` fallback prevents a crash, but it silently shows step content/title describing a *different* page than the one on screen. This is worse for privacy.html, terms.html, and 404.html specifically — TOUR_STEPS (lines 7-42) has zero entries for those three pages, so landing there mid-tour always renders body-centered content mismatched to what's visible. Fix suggestion: have the resume path call tourGoTo(idx) instead of renderTourStep(idx) directly, so the existing page-match/redirect logic applies uniformly to both programmatic and page-load resume. [low] tour.js:337 initTour() has no reentry guard. ensureTourOverlay() (line 86-98) is itself idempotent for the DOM node, but the three `document.addEventListener` calls for click/resize/keydown (lines 340-346, 362-367, 369-375) are registered unconditionally every call with no "already initialized" check — unlike cmdk.js's renderCmdk() which explicitly early-returns if `#cmdk` already exists (cmdk.js:89). Currently safe because bootSite() (script.js:770-804) only runs once per page load and initTour() is called exactly once from it (script.js:795), so this is latent rather than active. If initTour() were ever invoked a second time on the same document (future SPA-style re-init, dev-console call, etc.), all three listeners would double-fire — e.g. one ArrowRight press would call tourAdvance() twice, skipping a step. Fix suggestion: add a guard flag (e.g. `if (window.__tourInitialized) return; window.__tourInitialized = true;`) at the top of initTour(), matching the defensive pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase (renderCmdk). [nit] tour.js — resumed tour state (TOUR_LS_ACTIVE/TOUR_LS_INDEX, localStorage) has no timestamp or staleness check. A tour abandoned mid-way (tab closed without hitting Finish/Close) will auto-resume on the visitor's *next* visit regardless of how much time has passed — could be the same session or months later. May be intended "pick up where you left off" UX; flagging in case it isn't, since there's no explicit expiry. ── What I did NOT re-check (per task scope / verify.py coverage) ── JS syntax, tag balance, id/href integrity, and the static-vs-generated content equality that check_search_index_sync() (scripts/verify.py:247-272) already performs at commit time — none of that is duplicated above; all findings here are runtime/behavioral.
